subject: Mark Cuban says your 401(k) is the problem
preheader: He's half right. Plus: Ray Dalio on the one asset guaranteed to lose, and how to beat a denied Medicare claim.
greeting: Good morning. A billionaire picked a fight with the health insurers this week and told you to check your retirement account. Another one told you your savings account is a mistake. Both are pointing at something real. Today's issue sorts the useful half of each from the half that would cost you money.
today: Mark Cuban says your 401(k) is "part of the health care problem." He's half right, and the wrong half is the half that can help you
Ray Dalio says cash is the one asset guaranteed to lose you money. He's right, and most retirees hold it in the worst possible place
A denied Medicare claim is not the last word. The deadlines and steps that get most denials overturned

headline.title: Insurers count on you not appealing
headline.stat_label: of Medicare Advantage prior-authorization denials that were appealed got overturned (KFF, 2023 data). Only about one in nine denials is ever appealed.
headline.text: A heart transplant patient lost coverage for her anti-rejection drug until a viral post reached Mark Cuban, whose pharmacy now supplies it for about $300. Most people don't get a billionaire. What they do get is an appeals process with deadlines that insurers hope you'll miss.

stories.why: If your 401(k) tracks the S&P 500 you own UnitedHealth, Cigna, CVS and Elevance whether you meant to or not. Selling the fund won't change a single denial. Using Cuban's pharmacy for generics and appealing every no is the fight you can actually win.

What $100 bought in 1970 costs about $850 today. A retiree still needs two to three years of spending in cash, but at 0.1% in a big-bank account it's losing every year. Treasury bills and high-yield accounts pay several percent with the same insurance.

Original Medicare gives you 120 days from the summary notice to ask for a redetermination. Medicare Advantage gives you 60 days, and the plan must answer within 30. A mismatched name or a wrong billing code is behind a large share of denials, and the provider's office can often fix it without an appeal.

quiz.q: If your Medicare Advantage plan denies a service, how long do you have to file an appeal?
quiz.explain: Medicare Advantage members have 60 days from the denial notice to request a reconsideration, and the plan must respond within 30 days for a service you haven't received yet (72 hours if your doctor says waiting could harm you). Original Medicare is more generous: 120 days from the date on your Medicare Summary Notice.
